chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from a man, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Ali ibn Uqbah, from Musa ibn Ukayl al-Numayri, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:

“Regarding iron: it is the adornment of the people of the Fire, and gold is the adornment of the people of Paradise. Allah made gold in this world an adornment for women, so He prohibited men from wearing it and from praying in it. And Allah made iron in this world an adornment of the jinn and the shayatin, so He prohibited the Muslim man from wearing it in salat, unless he is facing an enemy, in which case there is no harm in it.”

He said: I said to him, “Then a man while traveling may have a knife with him in his khuff, which he cannot do without, or fastened in his trousers, and a key which he fears would be lost if he put it down, or he may have at his waist a belt made of iron.” He said, “There is no harm in the knife and the belt for the traveler or at a time of necessity, and likewise the key if he fears loss and forgetfulness. And there is no harm in the sword and every weapon of war during battle. Other than that, salat is not permissible in anything made of iron, for it is impure and transformed.”
And we have already presented the narration of Ammar al-Sabati that whenever iron is in a covering, then there is no harm in praying with it.

key_terms.السِّلَاحِ: weaponry; instruments of war exempted during battle
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat; the ritual prayer whose validity is being addressed
key_terms.الْحَدِيدِ: iron; the material discussed in the ruling on what may be worn during salat
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler; one for whom an exception is mentioned
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: necessity; a condition allowing exemption from the normal rule
key_terms.غِلَافٍ: covering; an enclosure mentioned as affecting the ruling of iron
key_terms.نَجِسٌ: impure; the stated legal quality of iron in this narration

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear iron during salat in Shi'a hadith sources?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wearing iron during salat, stating that prayer in something made of iron is not permissible except in cases such as travel, necessity, or battle. It also mentions related exceptions for items such as a knife, key, belt, and weapons, and refers to another narration allowing iron when it is enclosed in a covering.
